name: Market entry

subjectOf.text: Because new hedge fund managers concentrate on highly complex and profitable instruments where pricing and valuation problems are most prevalent, it becomes very difficult for managers to guarantee investors standard or accurate pricing procedures.
subjectOf.abstract: Most of these new managers focus their attention on highly complex and profitable instruments where pricing and valuation issues are most prevalent. This trend can make it very difficult for hedge fund managers to guarantee their investors standard or accurate pricing procedures.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Hedge Fund Valuation Retailization, Regulation, and Investor Suitability (2009). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1428387
scope_conditions: for newly launched funds run by managers leaving large institutions

subjectOf.text: The Dodd-Frank Act is notable for what it omits: it does not break up the largest banks, does little to help smaller and regional banks compete, and because compliance is burdensome and expensive may actually have raised the barrier to entry into financial services.
subjectOf.abstract: It does little to help smaller and regional banks compete with the big banks. Because complying with regulation is burdensome and expensive, the Act may have raised the barrier for entry into the financial services industry.
subjectOf.citation: Painter and Kaal, Initial Reflections on an Evolving Standard Constraints on Risk Taking by Directors and Officers in (2010). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1558614

subjectOf.text: Anecdotal evidence suggests that Title IV of the Dodd-Frank Act more than doubled the market entry threshold requirements for smaller hedge fund advisers.
subjectOf.abstract: Anecdotal evidence suggests that Title IV more than doubled the market entry threshold requirements for smaller hedge fund advisers.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: market entry for new hedge fund advisers after the Dodd-Frank Act

subjectOf.text: Before Title IV, launching a hedge fund could be accomplished by raising roughly $25 to $50 million, whereas after the Dodd-Frank Act the required initial amount may have risen to around $100 million.
subjectOf.abstract: Setting up a hedge fund before the enactment of Title IV could be accomplished by raising around $25-50 million. After the enactment of the Dodd-Frank Act, this number may have increased to around $100 million.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: comparison of pre and post Dodd-Frank Act market entry

subjectOf.text: The long-term effect of the Dodd-Frank Act on the private investment fund industry is likely to be characterized by increasing additional expenses and associated barriers to entry for new market entrants.
subjectOf.abstract: Given these survey results, it seems possible that the long- term effect of the Dodd-Frank Act on the private investment fund industry is characterized by increasing additional expenses and associated levels of barriers to entry for market entrants.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915
scope_conditions: inference from respondent forecasts for the next five years

subjectOf.text: Lower operating costs enabled by blockchain platform models will especially enable new and future managers to enter the market because start up and compliance costs can be significantly reduced.
subjectOf.abstract: the lower operating costs enabled by the platform models will especially enable new and future managers to enter the market because the start-up costs and compliance costs can be significantly reduced.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Applications and Fee Structure Developments in Private Investment Funds (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2959730
scope_conditions: platform models with low set up requirements and low running costs

subjectOf.text: The proposed DAO design is likely to lower barriers to entry in insurance, since non traditional firms and even individual investors can buy tokens at auction and then either underwrite with them or hold them passively.
subjectOf.abstract: In addition, the particular design outlined above is likely to facilitate the entry of new players to the insurance market. It is possible for a DAO to allow the participation of non-traditional firms and even individual investors.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Decentralized Underwriting (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396542

subjectOf.text: The compliance burden attached to operating an alternative trading system, including fees, consumer protection, examination, and books and records requirements, is typically cost prohibitive for startups.
subjectOf.abstract: ATS compliance costs are typically cost prohibitive for startups.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Samuel Evans, Blockchain-Based Securities Offerings (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3411110
scope_conditions: startup firms seeking to operate an ATS
